chunks: From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Souls are grouped in batches; they meet and recognize each other like horses recognize one another. Those that are familiar with each other unite, and those that are unfamiliar differ. And if a believer were to enter a mosque filled with many people, among whom there was only one other believer, his soul would incline towards that believer until he sat beside him.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of spiritual affinity between believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates the concept of 'Arwah Jundun Mujannada' (souls as organized troops), a metaphysical principle in Shia theology suggesting that spiritual affinity is innate and transcends physical proximity. This hadith underscores the ontological unity of the faithful, where the soul's inclination toward like-minded believers serves as a divine mechanism for social cohesion and spiritual recognition within the community.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 89. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:

Souls are grouped in batches; they look out for each other like horses. They feel familiar with those whom they know well and disagree with those whom they disapprove of. If a believer entered a mosque filled with people amongst whom there was but one another believer, his soul would incline towards that believer until he would go and sit beside him.
